F1.label: F1
F1.text: [F1] The screen $\mathscr S=\ell^\perp/\mathbb R\ell$ has a positive metric; $A_\lambda$ is the screen Jacobi map, $B=A'A^{-1}$ is self-adjoint before its first focal instant, $\theta=\operatorname{tr}B$, and $\sigma=B-\frac12\theta\,\mathrm{id}$ ([[def-gr-fx-null-screen-geometry]]).

steps.text:
For each $X\in T_pS$, the variation field $J_X(\lambda)=dF_{(p,\lambda)}(X,0)$ is a Jacobi field by [F3]. Its screen class satisfies the screen Jacobi equation
$$A_\lambda''+\mathcal R_\ell A_\lambda=0,\qquad \mathcal R_\ell[X]:=[R(X,\ell)\ell],$$
because [F2]-[F4] give $D_\ell^2J_X=R(\ell,J_X)\ell=-R(J_X,\ell)\ell$. The screen projection is well-defined since changing $J_X$ by a multiple of $\ell$ changes $R(J_X,\ell)\ell$ by zero. Before the first focal instant $A_\lambda$ is invertible, so differentiating $B=A'A^{-1}$ gives
$$B' = A''A^{-1}-A'A^{-1}A'A^{-1}=-\mathcal R_\ell-B^2.$$
[F1, F2, F3, F4, given, algebra]

The null hypersurface normal makes $B$ self-adjoint by [F1]. In two screen dimensions write $B=\frac{\theta}{2}\mathrm{id}+\sigma$; then $\operatorname{tr}\sigma=0$ and
$$\operatorname{tr}(B^2)=\frac{\theta^2}{2}+\operatorname{tr}(\sigma^2)=\frac{\theta^2}{2}+|\sigma|_{\bar q}^2.$$
The last equality holds because $\sigma$ is self-adjoint on the positive screen. [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

At any point choose the local pair supplied by [F1] and set $n:=k/2$, so $g(\ell,n)=-1$; complete it by a $\bar q$-orthonormal screen basis $E_1,E_2$. In this basis the inverse metric is
$$g^{-1}=-\ell\otimes n-n\otimes\ell+E_1\otimes E_1+E_2\otimes E_2.$$
Contracting the curvature in [F2], the two null-pair terms in $\operatorname{Ric}(\ell,\ell)$ have repeated first or last slots and vanish by [F4], leaving
$$\operatorname{Ric}(\ell,\ell)=\sum_{A=1}^2g(R(E_A,\ell)\ell,E_A)=\operatorname{tr}\mathcal R_\ell.$$
[F1, F2, F4, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

F1.label: F1
F1.text:
[F1] The screen quotient has a positive metric, $\chi_\ell$ is symmetric,
and screen covariant differentiation along an affine generator is
well-defined ([[def-gr-fx-null-screen-geometry]]).

steps.text:
Use the smooth tangent-bundle convention in [A1]. In a parallel
orthonormal screen frame, $\mathcal R$ has matrix entries
$\bar q(R(E_A,\ell)\ell,E_B)$. The curvature symmetries [F2] make this
matrix symmetric, and $\chi_\ell$ is symmetric by [F1]. Each term in $I$ is
therefore bilinear and independent of the representative in
$\ell^\perp/\mathbb R\ell$; changing a representative by a multiple of
$\ell$ leaves the screen class and the screen connection unchanged. The
contractions are invariant under orthonormal screen-frame changes, so $I$ is
a well-defined symmetric bilinear form. [F1, F2, A1, algebra]

For a smooth variation $F_s$, put $T=\partial_\lambda F_s$ and
$Z=\partial_sF_s$. Torsion-freeness gives $D_sT=D_\lambda Z$. The first
variation is
$$E'(s)=[g(Z,T)]_0^L-\int_0^L g(Z,D_\lambda T)\,d\lambda.$$
At $s=0$, $T=\ell$, $D_\lambda T=0$, $Z(L)=0$, and $Z(0)$ is tangent to
$S$ and orthogonal to $\ell$, so $E'(0)=0$. Differentiating once more and
using $[D_s,D_\lambda]T=R(Z,T)T$ gives, at $s=0$,
$$E''(0)=[g(D_sZ,\ell)]_0^L+ \int_0^L\bigl(|D_\ell Z|^2- g(R(Z,\ell)\ell,Z)\bigr)\,d\lambda.$$
Here the boundary terms $[g(Z,D_\ell Z)]_0^L$ from differentiation and
integration by parts cancel. The final endpoint contribution is zero because
$F_s(L)$ is fixed. At the initial endpoint, let $X=Z(0)\in T_pS$; along
$\alpha(s)=F_s(0)\in S$ one has $g(\alpha'(s),\ell(\alpha(s)))=0$. Differentiating
this identity gives $g(D_sZ(0),\ell)=-\chi_\ell(X,X)$, so the initial
boundary contribution in the bracket is $+\chi_\ell(X,X)$. Substitution
proves $E''(0)=I(Z,Z)$. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

The field realization in step 3.1 and the second-variation calculation
in step 2.1 establish the statement for every admissible $V$; symmetry and
well-definedness were proved in step 1.1. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 2.1,
step 3.1] ∎

F1.label: F1
F1.text:
[F1] On the positive screen $\ell^\perp/\mathbb R\ell$, the null second
fundamental form is symmetric and its endomorphism is
$B_0=q^{-1}\chi_\ell$ ([[def-gr-fx-null-screen-geometry]]).

F3.label: F3
F3.text:
[F3] The symmetric screen index form with the $+\chi_\ell$ initial boundary
term equals the energy second variation for variations starting on $S$ and
ending at $\gamma(L)$; every admissible screen field is realized by such a
variation ([[lem-gr-fx-null-screen-index-form]]).

steps.text:
Choose a parallel orthonormal frame of the positive screen along the
geodesic segment and write $\mathcal R[X]:=[R(X,\ell)\ell]$. The focal field
$J$ satisfies $J''+\mathcal RJ=0$ in this frame. Its screen derivative
$J'(\lambda_0)$ is nonzero: otherwise its zero value and derivative at
$\lambda_0$ would force $J$ to vanish identically by [F2], contrary to [A1].
The screen initial data are $J(0)=X\in T_pS$ and $J'(0)=B_0X$, so
$\langle J'(0),X\rangle=\chi_\ell(X,X)$. [F1, F2, F3, A1, construct]

Fix $L>\lambda_0$ sufficiently close to $\lambda_0$. On $[0,L]$ let
$Y=J$ up to $\lambda_0$ and $Y=0$ after $\lambda_0$. This continuous
piecewise-smooth screen field has $Y(0)=X$ and $Y(L)=0$. Let $I$ be the
screen index form supplied by [F3]. Its displayed formula extends
continuously to piecewise-smooth $H^1$ fields: in a parallel frame the
curvature coefficients are bounded on $[0,L]$, the integral terms are
continuous in $H^1$, and the endpoint trace is continuous because
$$|V(0)|\le L^{-1/2}\|V\|_{L^2}+L^{1/2}\|D_\ell V\|_{L^2},$$
obtained by integrating $V(0)=V(t)-\int_0^tD_\ell V\,d\lambda$ over
$0\le t\le L$. Thus $I(Y,Y)$ is defined. Integrating the Jacobi equation on
$[0,\lambda_0]$ gives
$$I(Y,Y)=\langle J'(\lambda_0),J(\lambda_0)\rangle- \langle J'(0),X\rangle+\chi_\ell(X,X)=0,$$
since the screen value at $\lambda_0$ is zero and
$\langle J'(0),X\rangle=\chi_\ell(X,X)$. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, algebra]

Choose a smooth screen field $W$ supported in a small interval about
$\lambda_0$, zero at both endpoints, and with
$W(\lambda_0)=-J'(\lambda_0)$. Integration by parts on each side of
$\lambda_0$ yields
$$I(Y,W)=\langle J'(\lambda_0),W(\lambda_0)\rangle =-|J'(\lambda_0)|^2<0.$$
Therefore $I(Y+\delta W,Y+\delta W)<0$ for sufficiently small $\delta>0$.
In the parallel frame, smooth the single derivative corner of $Y$ on
$[\lambda_0-\epsilon,\lambda_0+\epsilon]$ by a cubic interpolant matching
the values and first derivatives at the two endpoints, leaving the field
unchanged near $0$ and $L$. Since $Y$ is continuous and piecewise smooth,
the interpolant and its derivative stay bounded as $\epsilon\downarrow0$;
the $H^1$ error tends to zero because its support has length $2\epsilon$.
Adding $\delta W$ preserves smoothness, so continuity of $I$ gives a smooth
field $V$ with $V(0)\in T_pS$, $V(L)=0$ and $I(V,V)<0$. [F1, F2, F3,
step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

By [F3], this smooth field is realized by a curve variation $F_s$ with
$F_s(0)\in S$, $F_s(L)=\gamma(L)$, and screen variational field $V$; its
energy satisfies $E''(0)=I(V,V)<0$. The first-variation formula gives
$E'(0)=[g(V,\ell)]_0^L=0$, since the final point is fixed and the initial
field is tangent to $S$ and orthogonal to $\ell$. Also $E(0)=0$ because
$\gamma$ is null. The pointwise first derivative of
$g(\partial_\lambda F_s,\partial_\lambda F_s)$ vanishes because
$D_\lambda\ell=0$ and $V$ is a screen field. Hence, uniformly on the compact
interval,
$$g(\partial_\lambda F_s,\partial_\lambda F_s) =s^2h(\lambda)+O(s^3),\qquad \int_0^Lh(\lambda)\,d\lambda=I(V,V)<0.$$
[F1, F3, step 3.1, algebra]

Here is the longitudinal correction that turns this negative index into
a causal curve with a timelike subcurve. Choose a parallel null field $n$
along $\gamma$ with $g(\ell,n)=-1$, and extend $n$ smoothly to the nearby
curves in the local exponential charts; write $n_s(\lambda)$ for the
extension, with $n_0(\lambda)=n(\lambda)$. Use the exponential maps along a
finite subdivision of the compact geodesic segment to define the corrected
variation
$$\widetilde F_s(\lambda):= \exp_{F_s(\lambda)}\!\bigl(s^2a_s(\lambda)n_s(\lambda)\bigr),$$
where $F_s$ is the endpoint-fixed variation from step 4.1.
Choose
a smooth function $w\ge0$, supported in the short interval about
$\lambda_0$ contained in one convex normal neighborhood, positive on a
smaller interval, and normalized by $\int_0^Lw=-I(V,V)$. Add the displacement
$s^2a_s(\lambda)n(\lambda)$, with $a_s(0)=0$, and choose its derivative so
the corrected squared velocity of $\widetilde F_s$ is exactly
$-s^2c w(\lambda)$ for a scalar $c>0$. Divide the squared-velocity equation
by $s^2$; its derivative with respect to $a_s'$ at $s=0$ is
$2g(\ell,n)=-2$, so it remains nonzero for small $s$ and determines
$a_s'$ smoothly. At second order the equation is
$a_s'=(h+cw)/2+O(s)$, and hence
$$a_s(L)=\frac12\left(I(V,V)+c\int_0^Lw\right)+O(s).$$
At $c=1$ the leading term vanishes; for fixed small $\eta>0$, $a_s(L)$ has
opposite signs at $c=1-\eta$ and $c=1+\eta$ for all sufficiently small
$s$. Continuity therefore gives some
$c_s\in(1-\eta,1+\eta)$ with $a_s(L)=0$. The correction fixes both
endpoints; its initial displacement is zero, so the initial point still
lies on $S$. The corrected curve is future causal because its velocity is
close to $\ell$, and it is strictly timelike where $w>0$. [F1, F3, F7, F8,
step 4.1, construct, algebra]

F1.label: F1
F1.text:
[F1] On the positive screen, $\chi_\ell(X,Y)=g(\nabla_X\ell,Y)$,
$\theta=\operatorname{tr}_q\chi$, and the screen Jacobi map detects focal
instants ([[def-gr-fx-null-screen-geometry]]).

F2.label: F2
F2.text:
[F2] For an affine twist-free null congruence,
$\theta'=-\theta^2/2-|\sigma|^2-\operatorname{Ric}(\ell,\ell)$; under
$\operatorname{Ric}(\ell,\ell)\ge0$ and $\theta(0)<0$, the focal bound is
$2/|\theta(0)|$ ([[prop-gr-fx-null-raychaudhuri]]).

F3.label: F3
F3.text:
[F3] A focal point on a future null normal generator is followed immediately
by points in $I^+(S)$ ([[lem-gr-fx-null-focal-boundary-exclusion]]).

steps.text:
On $S$, $q=R^2d\Omega^2$. For tangent $X,Y$, flat-space differentiation
gives $\nabla_X\partial_r=X/R$ and $\nabla_X\partial_t=0$. Therefore
$\chi_\ell=q/R$ and $\chi_k=-q/R$, and since the screen dimension is two,
$\theta_\ell=2/R$ and $\theta_k=-2/R$. Direct inner products give
$g(\ell,\ell)=g(k,k)=0$ and $g(\ell,k)=-1-1=-2$; both fields are future
because their $t$ components are $1$. [A1, F1, construct, algebra]

In Cartesian coordinates the inward geodesic is
$\gamma_\omega(\lambda)=(\lambda,(R-\lambda)\omega)$. Varying $\omega$ in a
tangent direction $X\in T_{R\omega}(R\mathbb S^2)$ gives the Jacobi field
$J_X(\lambda)=(1-\lambda/R)X$. Its screen map is therefore
$A_\lambda=(1-\lambda/R)\operatorname{id}$ for $0\le\lambda<R$, with first
rank loss at $R$. Hence $B=-\operatorname{id}/(R-\lambda)$,
$\theta=-2/(R-\lambda)$, $\sigma=0$, and $\operatorname{Ric}=0$. Differentiating
$\theta$ verifies the equation in [F2], and
$2/|\theta(0)|=2/(2/R)=R$, so the comparison bound is sharp. [A1, F1, F2,
step 1.1, algebra]

Fix $R<\lambda<3R$. The point $p_-= (0,-R\omega)\in S$ and
$q_\lambda=\gamma_\omega(\lambda)$ have time separation $\lambda$ and spatial
separation
$$|(R-\lambda)\omega-(-R\omega)|=|2R-\lambda|<\lambda.$$
The straight segment from $p_-$ to $q_\lambda$ is future timelike because
its time component is positive and its squared interval is
$-\lambda^2+(2R-\lambda)^2<0$. Thus $q_\lambda\in I^+(S)$. This agrees with
[F3], which applies since $\lambda>R$ is immediately beyond the first focal
instant. [A1, F3, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

F1.label: F1
F1.text:
[F1] Under a normal-frame boost, $\chi_\ell$, $\theta_\ell$ and
$\sigma_\ell$ scale by $e^f$; the optical map and expansion are defined on
the positive screen ([[def-gr-fx-null-screen-geometry]]).

F2.label: F2
F2.text:
[F2] The affine screen equation is
$\theta'=-\theta^2/2-|\sigma|^2-\operatorname{Ric}(\ell,\ell)$ and the bound
is $2/|\theta(0)|$ when $\theta(0)<0$ and $\operatorname{Ric}(\ell,\ell)\ge0$
([[prop-gr-fx-null-raychaudhuri]]).

F3.label: F3
F3.text:
[F3] The focal event is geometric and every point of the normal generator
sufficiently just beyond it lies in $I^+(S)$, hence outside $E^+(S)$
([[lem-gr-fx-null-focal-boundary-exclusion]]).

steps.text:
Since $e^f>0$, the boost preserves the future null rays, and
$g(\ell',k')=e^fe^{-f}g(\ell,k)=-2$. The boost law in [F1] gives
$\widehat\theta_0=e^f\theta_0$, so $\widehat\theta_0$ has the same sign as $\theta_0$.
The new tangent is $\ell'=d/d\lambda'$, while $\ell=d/d\lambda$; solving
$d\lambda/d\lambda'=e^f$ with both parameters zero at the initial section
gives $\lambda'=e^{-f}\lambda$ because $f$ is constant along the generator.
[A1, F1, algebra]

Since $d/d\lambda'=e^f d/d\lambda$, [F1] gives
$\widehat B=e^fB$, $\widehat\sigma=e^f\sigma$, and
$\widehat\theta=e^f\theta$. Therefore
$d\widehat\theta/d\lambda'=e^{2f}d\theta/d\lambda$ and
$|\widehat\sigma|^2=e^{2f}|\sigma|^2$. Tensoriality gives
$\operatorname{Ric}(\ell',\ell')=e^{2f}\operatorname{Ric}(\ell,\ell)$.
Multiplying the Raychaudhuri equation in [F2] by $e^{2f}$ proves its form is
unchanged. If $\theta_0<0$, then
$$\lambda'_* =\frac2{|\widehat\theta_0|} =e^{-f}\frac2{|\theta_0|}=e^{-f}\lambda_*.$$
[F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

The screen Jacobi map is reparametrized by
$\widehat A_{\lambda'}=A_{e^f\lambda'}$, so its rank-loss event is the same point
of $M$ and its parameter value is multiplied by $e^{-f}$. By [F3], the
geometric statement that points just beyond that event lie in $I^+(S)$ is
unchanged by relabeling the affine parameter. Thus only the numerical affine
label changes; the causal-boundary conclusion does not. [F1, F3, step 1.1,
step 2.1, algebra] ∎

F8.label: F8
F8.text: [F8] [[def-gr-fx-null-screen-geometry]]: on a patch with a smooth future null normal $\ell$, $\theta_\ell=\operatorname{tr}_q\chi_\ell$, where $\chi_\ell(X,Y)=g(\nabla_X\ell,Y)$; a positive boost $\ell\mapsto e^f\ell$ sends $\theta_\ell$ to $e^f\theta_\ell$.

F10.label: F10
F10.text: [F10] [[prop-gr-fx-null-raychaudhuri]]: along a smooth null normal congruence with $\operatorname{Ric}(\ell,\ell)\ge0$ and $\theta(0)<0$, a focal instant occurs by affine parameter $2/|\theta(0)|$ if the congruence exists through that parameter.

F11.label: F11
F11.text: [F11] [[lem-gr-fx-null-focal-boundary-exclusion]]: a focal instant on a future null geodesic normal to $S$ puts all sufficiently close later points on that generator in $I^+(S)$, provided the geodesic and variation data continue slightly past the focal instant.

steps.text: For each point of $S$, choose a neighborhood with the two smooth null normal branches supplied by [F9]. On each branch rescale by a positive smooth factor so that $g(\ell,N)=-1$; this is possible by [F20] and does not change the sign of the expansion by [F8]. Both normalized expansions are continuous and negative at the chosen point by the trapped-surface hypothesis. Shrink the neighborhood so that both are at most $-c_j$ for some $c_j>0$. Compactness of $S$ gives a finite subcover; the minimum of its finitely many positive constants gives $c>0$ such that every normalized future null normal has initial expansion $\theta_0\le -c$. [A2, F8, F9, F20, given, choose]

Set $L:=2/c$. For each normalized null normal at $s\in S$, future completeness [F21] and smooth dependence [F16] give a smooth null normal geodesic congruence near that initial datum through $[0,L]$. Applying [F10] with $\theta_0\le-c$ and the null Ricci hypothesis gives a first focal parameter $\lambda_f\le 2/|\theta_0|\le L$. The extension required in [F11] is supplied by future null completeness, so its local variation data also exist slightly beyond $\lambda_f$. [A2, F10, F11, F16, F21, step 1.2, given]

Return to $p\in E^+(S)$ and its normal generator from steps 3.2, 4.1, and 5.1, with endpoint parameter $\lambda_p$. If a focal instant $\lambda_f$ occurred strictly before $\lambda_p$, [F11] would give a point $r=\gamma(\lambda)$ with $\lambda_f<\lambda<\lambda_p$ and $r\in I^+(S)$. Since $r\le p$, [F15] would imply $p\in I^+(S)$, a contradiction. Hence $\lambda_p\le\lambda_f\le L$; for $p\in S$ the parameter is $0$ and the same bound holds. [F11, F15, step 3.2, step 4.1, step 5.1, step 2.2, given]

Choose finitely many relatively compact coordinate patches covering $S$, each contained in a patch with the two smooth normalized null normal fields from step 1.2. Their compact closures $K_j$ exist by choosing smaller Euclidean chart balls and applying Heine–Borel [F19] and the continuous-image theorem [F17]. For each $K_j$ and each branch $\ell_{j,\pm}$, the parameter domain $K_j\times[0,L]$ is compact by [F22], and the map $(s,\lambda)\mapsto\exp_s(\lambda\ell_{j,\pm}(s))$ is continuous on it by [F16] and future completeness. Its image is compact by [F17]. A finite union of compact sets is compact, so the union $C$ of these images is compact. Step 6.1 shows that every $p\in E^+(S)$ lies in $C$. [F9, F11, F16, F17, F19, F22, step 1.2, step 6.1, given, construct]

F1.label: F1
F1.text: [F1] [[def-gr-fx-trapped-surface-and-black-region]]: $\theta_\ell=\operatorname{tr}_q\chi_\ell$ with $\chi_\ell(X,Y)=g(\nabla_X\ell,Y)$, and a future trapped surface requires both future null expansions to be negative.

F3.label: F3
F3.text: [F3] [[def-gr-fx-null-screen-geometry]]: the null second fundamental form is traced with the positive induced metric $q$ on the spacelike two-surface.

F5.label: F5
F5.text: [F5] [[lem-gr-fx-trapped-boundary-compactness]]: its compact-horismos conclusion assumes a compact future trapped surface, so the expansion signs computed here decide whether this particular sphere meets that prerequisite.

F6.label: F6
F6.text: [F6] [[thm-gr-fx-penrose-incompleteness]]: its incompleteness conclusion likewise assumes a compact future trapped surface; it cannot be applied with this sphere when one future expansion is positive.

steps.text: For angular coordinate fields $E_A$, the Christoffel formula [F4] gives $\Gamma^B{}_{rA}=\frac12(r^{-2}\gamma^{BC})(2r\gamma_{CA})=r^{-1}\delta^B_A$ and $\Gamma^\mu{}_{0A}=0$. Therefore on $r=R$, $\nabla_X\ell=R^{-1}X$ and $\nabla_Xk=-R^{-1}X$ for every tangent vector $X$ to $S$. [F2, F3, F4, given, algebra]

By [F1], $\chi_\ell=R^{-1}q$ and $\chi_k=-R^{-1}q$. Since $S$ is two-dimensional, tracing with $q$ gives $\theta_\ell=2/R>0$ and $\theta_k=-2/R<0$. Thus the pair of strict negative inequalities required for trapping fails. [F1, F3, step 1.2, given, algebra]
The positive expansion means this sphere does not supply the trapped-surface premise in [F5] or [F6]. The calculation makes no assertion about other surfaces in Minkowski space. [F5, F6, step 2.1] ∎

F3.label: F3
F3.text: [F3] [[def-gr-fx-trapped-surface-and-black-region]] and [[def-gr-fx-null-screen-geometry]]: a future trapped surface has both future null expansions negative; $\theta_\ell=\operatorname{tr}_q\chi_\ell$ with $\chi_\ell(X,Y)=g(\nabla_X\ell,Y)$.

F10.label: F10
F10.text: [F10] [[lem-gr-fx-trapped-boundary-compactness]]: under Countable Choice and Dependent Choice, global hyperbolicity, a compact future trapped surface, null Ricci nonnegativity, and future null completeness, $E^+(S)$ is compact.

F11.label: F11
F11.text: [F11] [[thm-gr-fx-penrose-incompleteness]]: under AC, global hyperbolicity, a compact future trapped surface, and null Ricci nonnegativity, the incompleteness conclusion also requires a connected noncompact smooth spacelike Cauchy hypersurface.

steps.text: The mixed Christoffel symbols in [F2] give $\nabla_X\partial_\tau=(a'/a)X$ and $\nabla_X\partial_\chi=(\partial_\chi r/r)X=(\cot\chi)X$ for every angular tangent vector $X$. Thus at $\chi=\pi/2$, $\chi_\ell=(a'/a)q_S$ and $\chi_k=(a'/a)q_S$. Tracing in two dimensions gives $\theta_\ell=\theta_k=2a'/a=2H\tanh(H\tau_0)<0$. So $S_{\tau_0}$ is future trapped by [F3]. [F2, F3, step 1.5, algebra]

The spacetime is globally hyperbolic by step 2.1, has the compact trapped surface of step 2.3, satisfies the null Ricci condition by step 2.2, and is future null complete by step 1.4. By [F9] and the assumed AC, the choice hypotheses of [F10] also hold, so [F10] gives compactness of $E^+(S_{\tau_0})$, consistently with the compact Cauchy slices in step 1.2. [A1, F9, F10, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 1.4, step 2.3]

By [F13], applied to the complete timelike product flow $\Psi$ from step 1.1 and the compact slice $\Sigma_0$ from step 1.2, every smooth spacelike Cauchy hypersurface of $M_H$ is diffeomorphic to $\Sigma_0$ and hence compact. The model satisfies AC, global hyperbolicity, the compact trapped-surface, and null-Ricci hypotheses of [F11], but has no connected noncompact smooth spacelike Cauchy hypersurface. It is therefore outside the theorem’s scope while remaining future null complete; the noncompact-Cauchy condition cannot simply be omitted. [A1, F9, F11, F13, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 1.4, step 2.3] ∎

F5.label: F5
F5.text: [F5] [[def-gr-fx-null-screen-geometry]]: a null hypersurface has a null normal field tangent to it; its null generators are the integral curves of that field.

steps.text: Put $A=r^2+a^2$. In the ingoing chart the inverse metric has $g^{vr}=A/\Sigma$, $g^{\widetilde\phi r}=a/\Sigma$, and $g^{rr}=\Delta/\Sigma$. Thus on $H^+$, $\sharp_g(dr)=(A/\Sigma)\partial_v+(a/\Sigma)\partial_{\widetilde\phi}$ by [F9]. The stationary and axial fields remain $\partial_v$ and $\partial_{\widetilde\phi}$, so $\sharp_g(dr)=(A/\Sigma)(T+(a/A)\Phi)$. It follows that the null normal direction is $\chi=T+\Omega_H\Phi$ with $\Omega_H=a/(r_+^2+a^2)$. Equivalently, $\Delta(r_+)=0$ gives $2Mr_+=r_+^2+a^2$, and direct substitution yields $g(\chi,\chi)|_{r_+}=0$. [A1, F1, F2, F5, F9, step 2.1, algebra]

F1.label: F1
F1.text: [F1] In Bondi coordinates $(u,r,x^A)$, the metric has the Bondi-Sachs form and the determinant gauge is $\det\gamma=\det q$. Its angular expansion is $\gamma_{AB}=q_{AB}+C_{AB}/r+P_{AB}/r^2+O(r^{-3})$, with $q^{AB}C_{AB}=0$ and $q^{AB}P_{AB}=\tfrac12C_{AB}C^{AB}$; $V=r-2m+O(r^{-1})$, $N_{AB}=\partial_uC_{AB}$, and all coefficient remainders have the differentiated uniform bounds stated in [[def-gr-fx-bondi-expansion]].

steps.text: Metric compatibility and zero torsion give $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12g^{ad}(\partial_bg_{cd}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc})$: lower the output index in metric compatibility and add the two cyclic equations minus the third. Multiplication of the Bondi metric by $g^{ur}=-E^{-1}$, $g^{rr}=E^{-1}V/r$, $g^{rA}=-E^{-1}U^A$, $g^{AB}=h^{AB}$ and $g^{uu}=g^{uA}=0$ gives the identity matrix. Its determinant is $-E^2r^4\det q$. Differentiating a determinant gives $\Gamma^a{}_{ab}=\partial_b\log\sqrt{|\det g|}$, so the traces are exactly $T_u:=\Gamma^a{}_{au}=2\dot\beta$, $T_r:=\Gamma^a{}_{ar}=2/r+2\beta_r$ and $T_A:=\Gamma^a{}_{aA}=Q_A+2\beta_A$. In particular $\operatorname{tr}(\gamma^{-1}\dot\gamma)=0$ exactly; no trace-free part of $P_{AB}$ has been removed. Contracting [F3] using [F2] gives $\operatorname{Ric}_{bc}=\partial_a\Gamma^a{}_{bc}-\partial_cT_b+\Gamma^a{}_{bc}T_a-\Gamma^a{}_{cd}\Gamma^d{}_{ba}$. [F1, F2, F3, A1, algebra]

The given differentiated expansions imply $E=1+O(r^{-2})$, $h_{AB}=r^2q_{AB}+rC_{AB}+O(1)$, $h^{AB}=r^{-2}q^{AB}-r^{-3}C^{AB}+O(r^{-4})$, $g_{uu}=-1+2m/r+O(r^{-2})$ and $g_{uA}=-w_A+O(r^{-1})$. These follow directly from $g_{uu}=-EV/r+h_{AB}U^AU^B$ and $g_{uA}=-h_{AB}U^B$. A radial derivative lowers each remainder's order by one, and time or angular derivatives through total order two preserve its order. Products and inverses have these same differentiated bounds, since their denominators tend uniformly to nonzero ones. Every differentiated expression below uses at most two derivatives of the metric coefficients. Thus these are the existing differentiated hypotheses, not a termwise differentiability assumption beyond them. [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

For the radial constraint put $H^B{}_A:=\Gamma^B{}_{rA}$ and $T^r{}_A:=\Gamma^r{}_{rA}$. The Christoffel formula of step 1.1 gives the exact identities $\Gamma^u{}_{rA}=0$, $\Gamma^u{}_{rr}=\Gamma^B{}_{rr}=0$, $\Gamma^r{}_{rr}=2\beta_r$, $H^B{}_A=\tfrac12h^{BC}\partial_rh_{AC}$, and $T^r{}_A=\beta_A+(2E)^{-1}h_{AB}\partial_rU^B$. Hence $H^B{}_A=\delta^B_A/r-C^B{}_A/(2r^2)+O(r^{-3})$ and $T^r{}_A=-w_A/r+O(r^{-2})$. Also $\Gamma^u{}_{AB}=(2E)^{-1}\partial_rh_{AB}=O(r)$ and $\Gamma^B{}_{ru}=\tfrac12h^{BC}(\partial_rg_{uC}+\partial_CE)=O(r^{-4})$. The angular symbols are exactly $\Gamma^C{}_{AB}=\Gamma[\gamma]^C{}_{AB}+(2E)^{-1}U^C\partial_rh_{AB}$. Their difference from the round connection is $S^C{}_{AB}:=\Gamma^C{}_{AB}-\Gamma[q]^C{}_{AB}=\{D_AC^C{}_B+D_BC^C{}_A-D^CC_{AB}\}/(2r)+w^Cq_{AB}/r+O(r^{-2})$, obtained by inserting $\gamma=q+C/r+O(r^{-2})$ in its connection formula. Since $q^{AB}C_{AB}=0$, its contracted leading coefficient is $S^C{}_{AC}=w_A/r+O(r^{-2})$. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

For the supplementary coefficient, set $K^a{}_b:=\Gamma^a{}_{ub}$. Using the exact traces from step 1.1 and combining $\partial_AK^A{}_u+Q_AK^A{}_u=D_AK^A{}_u$, the Ricci formula is exactly $\operatorname{Ric}_{uu}=\partial_uK^u{}_u+\partial_rK^r{}_u+D_AK^A{}_u-2\ddot\beta+2\dot\beta K^u{}_u+(2/r+2\beta_r)K^r{}_u+2\beta_AK^A{}_u-K^a{}_bK^b{}_a$. The Christoffel formula gives $K^u{}_u=2\dot\beta+(2E)^{-1}\partial_rg_{uu}$ exactly. It also gives $K^r{}_u=-\dot m/r+O(r^{-2})$ and $K^A{}_u=-\dot w^A/r^2+O(r^{-3})$: the leading terms come respectively from $\tfrac12g^{ru}\partial_ug_{uu}$ and $h^{AB}\partial_ug_{uB}$, while all other terms have the indicated lower orders. Therefore $\partial_uK^u{}_u-2\ddot\beta=-\dot m/r^2+O(r^{-3})$, $\partial_rK^r{}_u=\dot m/r^2+O(r^{-3})$, $D_AK^A{}_u=-D_A\dot w^A/r^2+O(r^{-3})$ and $(2/r)K^r{}_u=-2\dot m/r^2+O(r^{-3})$. The remaining three terms involving a derivative of $\beta$ times a $K$ are $O(r^{-4})$. The remainder differentiations here are covered by step 2.1. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

Expand the contracted Ricci formula of step 1.1 for $(b,c)=(r,A)$. The angular derivative and background-connection terms combine into $D_BH^B{}_A$. The derivative $-\partial_AT_r=-2\partial_A\beta_r$ is $O(r^{-3})$. In the final quadratic sum, the only non-background terms possibly of order $r^{-2}$ are $S^C{}_{AB}H^B{}_C$ and $H^C{}_AT^r{}_C$: their coefficients are respectively $w_A$ and $-w_A$, by step 3.1, so they cancel. The other potentially large product $\Gamma^u{}_{AB}\Gamma^B{}_{ru}$ is $O(r^{-3})$; products with $\Gamma^u{}_{rA},\Gamma^u{}_{rr},\Gamma^B{}_{rr}$ vanish, and products involving $\beta_r$ or $\beta_A$ are $O(r^{-3})$ or smaller. Consequently $\operatorname{Ric}_{rA}=\partial_rT^r{}_A+D_BH^B{}_A+(2/r)T^r{}_A+O(r^{-3})=r^{-2}(-w_A-\tfrac12D_BC^B{}_A)+O(r^{-3})$. The first, second and third terms contribute respectively $w_A$, $-\tfrac12D_BC^B{}_A$ and $-2w_A$. Vacuum [A2] therefore gives $w^A=-\tfrac12D_BC^{AB}$ without determining $U^A_{(3)}$ or any trace-free coefficient of $P_{AB}$. [F1, F2, F3, A2, step 1.1, step 3.1, algebra]

To exhibit every possible quadratic contribution, the same Christoffel formula gives $K^u{}_r=0$, $K^u{}_A=\beta_A+(2E)^{-1}\partial_rg_{uA}=O(r^{-2})$, $K^r{}_r=O(r^{-2})$, $K^r{}_A=O(r^{-1})$, $K^A{}_r=O(r^{-4})$, and $K^A{}_B=\tfrac12h^{AC}\partial_uh_{BC}+O(r^{-2})=N^A{}_B/(2r)+O(r^{-2})$; also $K^u{}_u=O(r^{-2})$, $K^r{}_u=O(r^{-1})$ and $K^A{}_u=O(r^{-2})$ by step 3.2. Thus in $K^a{}_bK^b{}_a$ the $uu$ and $rr$ diagonal products are $O(r^{-4})$, the $ur$ pair vanishes, the $uA$ pair is $O(r^{-4})$, the $rA$ pair is $O(r^{-5})$, and only the angular block contributes at order $r^{-2}$, giving $K^A{}_BK^B{}_A=N_{AB}N^{AB}/(4r^2)+O(r^{-3})$. This exhausts the contraction, rather than omitting uncomputed subleading terms. [F1, F2, F3, step 2.1, step 3.2, algebra]

F1.label: F1
F1.text: [F1] $N_{AB}=\partial_uC_{AB}$ and the differentiated metric expansion gives a local leading screen perturbation $C_{AB}/r$ with a remainder whose first two retarded-time derivatives are $O(r^{-2})$ ([[def-gr-fx-bondi-expansion]]).

steps.text: Apply [F5] to each smooth tensor component $C_{AB}(u,x)$ at the fixed angular point. Since $N_{AB}=\partial_uC_{AB}$, $C_{AB}(u_2,x)-C_{AB}(u_1,x)=\int_{u_1}^{u_2}N_{AB}(u,x)\,du$. This is the first identity. [A1, F1, F5, given, algebra]

With $s'(u_1)=0$, integrate the first-order equation twice to obtain
$$s^A(u_2)-s^A(u_1)=\frac12\int_{u_1}^{u_2}(u_2-v)\,\partial_v^2H^A{}_B(v)\,s^B\,dv+O(\varepsilon^2|s|).$$
Integration by parts gives the integral as $\Delta H^A{}_B-(u_2-u_1)\partial_uH^A{}_B(u_1)$. The leading part of the endpoint derivative vanishes by $N_{AB}(u_1)=0$, and the remainder derivative is $O(r^{-2})$ by [F1]; hence its contribution is $O(r^{-2}|s|)$. Also $\Delta H^A{}_B=\Delta C^A{}_B/r+O(r^{-2})$ by [F1]. Substitution proves the stated leading displacement and both error orders. [A2, F1, step 1.2, algebra]

Integrating the first-order Jacobi equation once gives $\partial_us^A(u_2)=\tfrac12(\partial_uH^A{}_B(u_2)-\partial_uH^A{}_B(u_1))s^B+O(\varepsilon^2|s|)$. At both endpoints the leading derivative is $N^A{}_B/r=0$; the derivative of the remainder in [F1] is $O(r^{-2})$. This proves the endpoint velocity estimate. [A2, F1, step 1.2, algebra] ∎

F1.label: F1
F1.text: [F1] The unit round metric $q_{AB}$ is positive definite on every angular tangent plane, $d\Omega$ is its area form on the compact boundaryless sphere $S^2$, and the sphere covariant derivative is $D_A$ ([[def-gr-fx-bondi-expansion]]).

F2.label: F2
F2.text: [F2] The mass aspect obeys $\partial_um=\tfrac14D_AD_BN^{AB}-\tfrac18N_{AB}N^{AB}$ in the vacuum expansion ([[lem-gr-fx-bondi-mass-coefficient]]).

steps.text: For fixed $u\in I$, define the smooth sphere vector field $X^A:=D_BN^{AB}$. In standard spherical coordinates $q=d\theta^2+\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2$, its divergence satisfies $D_AX^A\,d\Omega=\{\partial_\theta(\sin\theta X^\theta)+\partial_\phi(\sin\theta X^\phi)\}\,d\theta\,d\phi$. The $\phi$-boundary terms cancel by periodicity. Smoothness makes $X^\theta$ bounded in norm near each pole, so $\sin\theta X^\theta\to0$ at $\theta=0,\pi$; hence $\int_{S^2}D_AD_BN^{AB}\,d\Omega=0$. [A1, F1, given, algebra]

Smoothness on each compact $u$-slab permits differentiation under the finite sphere integral: for small $h$, the difference quotient for $m_B$ equals $\frac1{4\pi}\int_{S^2}\int_0^1\partial_um(u+th,x)\,dt\,d\Omega$, and uniform continuity of $\partial_um$ makes it converge uniformly in $x$ to $\frac1{4\pi}\partial_um(u,x)$. Therefore $\frac{dm_B}{du}=\frac1{4\pi}\int_{S^2}\partial_um\,d\Omega$. [F1, given, algebra]

Substitute [F2] into step 1.2 and use step 1.1 to eliminate the double divergence. The remaining term is $-\frac1{32\pi}\int_{S^2}N_{AB}N^{AB}\,d\Omega$, proving the equality. Since $q$ is positive definite, $N_{AB}N^{AB}=|N|_q^2\ge0$ pointwise, proving the inequality. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

If $dm_B/du=0$ at a fixed $u\in J$, step 2.1 gives the integral of the continuous nonnegative function $|N|_q^2$ equal to zero. If $N$ were nonzero at some point, continuity and positive definiteness of $q$ would make $|N|_q^2$ strictly positive on a sphere neighborhood of positive area, contradicting the zero integral. Thus $N=0$ on that cut; applying this to every $u\in J$ proves the final claim. [F1, step 2.1, given, algebra] ∎

F1.label: F1
F1.text: [F1] $q_{AB}$ is positive definite, $D$ is its Levi-Civita derivative, and $d\Omega$ is the finite area measure on the unit sphere; a Bondi shear is a symmetric trace-free smooth sphere tensor and $N_{AB}=\partial_uC_{AB}$ ([[def-gr-fx-bondi-expansion]]).

F2.label: F2
F2.text: [F2] The local mass-aspect and integrated mass-loss equations are $\partial_um=\tfrac14D_AD_BN^{AB}-\tfrac18N_{AB}N^{AB}$ and $\Delta m_B=-\tfrac1{32\pi}\int N_{AB}N^{AB}\,du\,d\Omega$ ([[lem-gr-fx-bondi-mass-coefficient]], [[prop-gr-fx-bondi-mass-loss]]).

F3.label: F3
F3.text: [F3] If the news vanishes at both endpoints, an initially comoving screen Jacobi separation has leading change $\Delta s^A=\tfrac1{2r}\Delta C^A{}_Bs^B+O(r^{-2}|s|)+O(\varepsilon^2|s|)$ under the stated local approximation ([[prop-gr-fx-memory-integral]]).

steps.text: The scalar $Y$ is smooth because it is the restriction of a polynomial on $\mathbb R^3$. By contraction, $q^{AB}T_{AB}=D^2Y-\tfrac12(2)D^2Y=0$. In spherical coordinates at the equator $\theta=\pi/2$, $D_\theta D_\theta Y=3$, $D_\phi D_\phi Y=0$, and $D^2Y=3$, so $T_{\theta\theta}=3/2\ne0$. Thus $T$ is a nonzero smooth trace-free tensor. [A1, F1, given, algebra]

The fields $C_{AB}=aHT_{AB}$ and $N_{AB}=agT_{AB}$ are smooth and trace-free, and $N=\partial_uC$. Therefore $\Delta C_{AB}=aT_{AB}$ by the normalization $\int g=1$. Define $m(u,x)$ from $m(-1,x)=0$ by integrating the right side of the local mass-aspect equation in [F2]; its integrand is smooth, so this gives smooth formal Bondi mass-aspect data satisfying that constraint. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 1.2, A2, construct, algebra]

Applying [F2] over $[-1,1]$ gives the displayed mass change. The first integral is positive because $g$ is continuous and has unit integral; the sphere integral is positive because $q$ is positive definite and $T$ is continuous and nonzero by step 1.1. Since $a\ne0$, the mass change is strictly negative. [A2, F1, F2, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

The pulse has $N(-1)=N(1)=0$, so [F3] applies. Its integrated shear change is $\Delta C=aT$, hence the leading detector displacement is $\Delta s^A=\tfrac{a}{2r}T^A{}_Bs^B+O(r^{-2}|s|)+O(\varepsilon^2|s|)$, with exactly the stated finite-radius and nonlinear qualifications. [F3, step 2.1, A2, algebra] ∎

F1.label: F1
F1.text: [F1] The angular metric $q$ is positive definite, $D$ is its Levi-Civita derivative, and the news is $N_{AB}=\partial_uC_{AB}$ ([[def-gr-fx-bondi-expansion]]).

F2.label: F2
F2.text: [F2] In a fixed Bondi frame the infinitesimal shear action is $\delta_fC_{AB}=fN_{AB}-2D_AD_Bf+q_{AB}D^2f$ ([[def-gr-fx-bms-supertranslation]]).

F5.label: F5
F5.text: [F5] The shear difference is $\Delta C_{AB}=\int_{u_1}^{u_2}N_{AB}\,du$ and the leading detector displacement is proportional to $\Delta C_{AB}$ under the endpoint and large-radius hypotheses ([[prop-gr-fx-memory-integral]]).

steps.text: The restriction $Y=\tfrac12(3x_3^2-1)$ is smooth on the sphere because it is the restriction of a polynomial. Put $T_{AB}:=D_AD_BY-\tfrac12q_{AB}D^2Y$. Its trace is zero. At $\theta=\pi/2$, $D_\theta D_\theta Y=3$, $D_\phi D_\phi Y=0$ and $D^2Y=3$, so $T_{\theta\theta}=3/2$; hence $T$ is nonzero. [A1, F1, given, algebra]

Since $Y$ is independent of $u$, [F2] gives $C_{AB}=\delta_fC_{AB}=-2aT_{AB}$, independent of $u$ and nonzero; [F1] then gives $N_{AB}=0$. The data are formal infinitesimal boundary data, so no nonlinear finite transformation is asserted. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

Substitution of $N_{AB}=0$ in [F3] gives $\partial_um=0$, and [F4] gives $dm_B/du=0$. For every $u_1<u_2$, [F5] gives $\Delta C_{AB}=\int_{u_1}^{u_2}0\,du=0$ and hence zero leading memory displacement. Thus the static nonzero shear has no news flux and no shear change. [F3, F4, F5, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

F4.label: F4
F4.text: [F4] [[lem-gr-fx-trapped-boundary-compactness]]: under the stated trapped-surface, null Ricci, global-hyperbolicity, and future-null-completeness assumptions, $E^+(S)=\partial I^+(S)$ is a compact topological three-manifold without boundary.

steps.text: The restriction $T|_S$ is continuous and $S$ is nonempty compact, so [F8] gives a point $s_0\in S$ at which $T|_S$ is minimal. If $s_0\in I^+(S)$, some $s_1\in S$ satisfies $s_1\ll s_0$; since $T$ is temporal, [F6] gives $T(s_1)<T(s_0)$, contradicting minimality. Thus $s_0\notin I^+(S)$. As $s_0\in S\subseteq J^+(S)$ by reflexivity, $s_0\in E^+(S)$, so this boundary is nonempty. [F2, F4, F6, F8, step 2.1, given, contradiction]

The domain $E^+(S)$ is a topological three-manifold without boundary by [F4], and $S_0$ is a smooth three-manifold by [F2]. For each $x\in E^+(S)$, choose manifold charts about $x$ and $\pi(x)$ and shrink the source chart so its image lies in the target chart. In these coordinates $\pi$ is continuous and injective between open subsets of $\mathbb R^3$; [F7] makes its image open. Taking the union over $x$ shows $\pi(E^+(S))$ is open in $S_0$. [F2, F4, F7, step 3.3, construct]

By [F4], $E^+(S)$ is compact, and $\pi$ is continuous, so [F8] makes $\pi(E^+(S))$ compact. The smooth manifold $S_0$ is Hausdorff; [F9] therefore makes this image closed in $S_0$. [F2, F4, F8, F9, step 3.3]

Since $\Phi$ is Killing by [F3] and [F8], set $K^\Phi_{ab}:=\Phi_a\Phi_b$. The product rule gives $
abla_{(a}K^\Phi_{bc)}= rac13[\Phi_b(
abla_a\Phi_c+
abla_c\Phi_a)+\Phi_c(
abla_a\Phi_b+
abla_b\Phi_a)+\Phi_a(
abla_b\Phi_c+
abla_c\Phi_b)]=0$. Thus $K^\Phi$ is a reducible Killing tensor by [F4]. [F3, F4, F8, algebra]
By [F3], $\Omega_H=a/(r_+^2+a^2)$, so $\Omega_H=0$ at $a=0$. The vacuum statement follows by applying [F6] to this same metric and restricting its domain to $r>2M$. [given, F3, F6, step 1.1, algebra]

Because $T$ is spacelike by [F1], decompose it relative to $n$ as $T=\alpha n+w$, where $\alpha:=-g(T,n)$ and $w:=T+g(T,n)n\in n^\perp$. By [F2], if $\beta:=\sqrt{g(w,w)}$ then $\beta>|\alpha|$; set $e:=w/\beta$, so $g(e,e)=1$, $g(n,e)=0$, and $T=\alpha n+\beta e$. [given, A1, F1, F2, algebra]

F3.label: F3
F3.text: [F3] [[prop-gr-fx-kerr-horizon-generator]]: $H^+$ is null, $\chi=T+\Omega_H\Phi$ is its null normal generator, and $T,\Phi$ preserve the horizon.

steps.text:
Since $\chi$ is normal to the null hypersurface $H^+$ and both $T$ and $\Phi$ are tangent to it by [F3], $g(\chi,T)=g(\chi,\Phi)=0$ on $H^+$. Hence the metric-trace term in [F2] vanishes when contracted with $\chi^aT^b$, so
$Q(\chi,T)=(\chi\psi)(T\psi)$. [given, A1, F2, F3, algebra]

Along a stationary orbit, write $u(\tau)=A e^{-i\omega\tau}$ with constant $A$; [F1] gives
$T\psi=\operatorname{Re}(-i\omega u)$ and
$\chi\psi=\operatorname{Re}(-i(\omega-m\Omega_H)u)$. [given, F1, step 1.1, algebra]

On the compact patch $D$, smoothness bounds $|u|^2$ and the induced area density, so both displayed integrals are finite. Integrating step 3.1 gives the formula for $\mathcal F_D$. If $u|_D$ is not identically zero, continuity and density of the interior give an interior point where $|u|^2>0$ and a smaller coordinate disk where $|u|^2\ge b>0$. The positive smooth area density has a positive lower bound $a>0$ on a still smaller closed disk; its positive Euclidean area makes $\int_D|u|^2d\mu_D\ge ab\,\operatorname{area}(\text{disk})>0$. Step 4.1 then makes $\mathcal F_D<0$. Such patches exist locally at a nonzero mode point $p$. By [F3], $T_pH^+=\chi_p^\perp$ for a nonzero null normal $\chi_p$. Nondegeneracy gives $v$ with $g(\chi_p,v)=-1$; then $k=v+\tfrac12g(v,v)\chi_p$ is null and $g(\chi_p,k)=-1$. The plane spanned by $\chi_p,k$ has one negative and one positive direction, so its orthogonal complement is a positive two-plane in $T_pH^+$. Choose a smooth hypersurface chart whose first two coordinate vectors span that plane at $p$, fix its third coordinate, and shrink a closed coordinate disk about $p$. Positivity persists by continuity of its metric matrix, and the disk stays in the mode domain and the nonzero set. No integral over a full noncompact horizon is used. [given, F3, step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra] ∎

F1.label: F1
F1.text: [F1] [[def-gr-fx-kerr-horizon-mode]]: $\widetilde\omega=\omega-m\Omega_H$ for a smooth joint mode of $T$ and $\Phi$.

F2.label: F2
F2.text: [F2] [[lem-gr-fx-kerr-horizon-modal-flux]]: for a nonzero smooth mode trace with $\omega>0$, the averaged stationary horizon flux density is $\tfrac12\omega\widetilde\omega|u|^2$.

steps.text:
The chosen frequency satisfies $\omega=m\Omega_H/2>0$ and
$\widetilde\omega=\omega-m\Omega_H=-m\Omega_H/2<0$. [given, A1, A2, F1, algebra]

The horizon-flux identity [F2] gives $\langle Q(\chi,T)\rangle_T=\tfrac12\omega\widetilde\omega|u|^2=-(m\Omega_H)^2|u|^2/8$. This is nonpositive at every point, zero at nodes and strictly negative where $u\ne0$; being a nonzero mode does not exclude nodes. [given, A2, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

For a compact smooth spacelike cut patch $D$ meeting the nonzero set, [F2] proves $\int_D|u|^2d\mu_D>0$ and finiteness of that integral. Integrating step 2.1 therefore gives $\mathcal F_D=-(m\Omega_H)^2\int_D|u|^2d\mu_D/8<0$. Such small patches are supplied by the local cut construction in [F2]. The conclusion remains conditional on the given trace, without a global wave or scattering existence claim. [given, A2, F2, step 2.1, algebra] ∎
